title: Robot Privacy Research Earns CHI 2026 Honorable Mention
summary: The recognized paper asks how robots can respect older adults' privacy as preferences and circumstances change.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post

paragraphs.text: A paper coauthored by Chorong Park received an Honorable Mention at CHI 2026. Park announced the recognition on March 9; Purdue's subsequent conference report independently confirms the award for "Privacy is Not One-Click: Designing Robots That Adapt to Older Adults' Changing Boundaries."

Park described a community-engaged project that began in summer 2024 and included two participatory design workshops in an assisted-living setting. Interviews, storyboards, and discussion helped the team explore how privacy expectations shift over time and across relationships.

The work challenges the idea that a single agreement can settle privacy for the life of a robotic system. Instead, the team considered ways to make privacy preferences adjustable and understandable as people's needs change.

Park's reflection points to design possibilities such as adaptable privacy profiles, real-time feedback, and greater control over personal data. These are research-informed design directions, rather than an announcement of a finished privacy product.
